issues.legal_issue: Income from a deceased person's estate remains assessable in the hands of the person administering it until the estate has been distributed to the beneficiaries according to their interests.
material_facts: The will left the deceased's property to two beneficiaries and named no executor; the deceased's son took charge of and administered the estate.
The estate was not distributed to the beneficiaries during the assessment years in dispute, and the Tribunal found that nothing was distributed until a later date.
The estate included movable and immovable property requiring division and a share in a firm whose devolution to the beneficiaries had not been shown.
The income from the estate had previously been assessed in the hands of the person administering it.
issues.conclusion: The administration had not been completed during the relevant years, so the income was assessable in the hands of the person administering the estate, not as the beneficiaries' income. The appeals were allowed and the question was answered in favour of the assessee.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 168(1) and (3) of the Income Tax Act, 1961, the estate's income is assessed in the hands of the executor, and that assessment continues for the period up to distribution to the beneficiaries according to their interests; section 168's explanation includes an administrator or other person administering the estate. Section 168(3) reflects the pre-existing law described in Raghavalu Naidu & Sons v. C.I.T.: executors must administer the estate, satisfy its obligations, ascertain the residue, and hand it over; a residuary beneficiary's interest in the residue does not become absolute until it is ascertained and distribution or appropriation occurs. The Court also referred to Lord Sudeley v. Attorney-General, Barnardo's Homes v. Special Income Tax Commissioners, Attenborough v. Solomon, C.I.T. v. Bakshi Sampuran Singh, and C.I.T. v. Ghosh.

predicates.income_tax_estate_income_proceeding: The proceeding concerned income-tax assessment of income arising from a deceased person's estate.
predicates.administrator_administered_estate: A person took charge of and administered the deceased person's estate.
predicates.estate_not_distributed: The estate had not been distributed to the beneficiaries according to their interests during the period at issue.
predicates.estate_income_assessed_to_administrator: The income from the estate is assessed to the person administering it.

issues.definition: When an income-tax proceeding concerns estate income, a person administered the estate, and distribution to the beneficiaries had not occurred, the estate income is assessed to that administrator.

issues.legal_issue: Outstanding estate-duty liability must be considered when deciding whether administration of an estate is complete.
material_facts: Part of the estate duty assessed on the property passing on the deceased's death remained unpaid during the relevant period.
The person administering the estate was an accountable person for the estate duty, and a substantial part of the duty had been paid without delay.
The record did not show deliberate delay in paying the balance or in distributing the estate.
issues.conclusion: The outstanding estate-duty liability could not simply be ignored in deciding whether administration was complete; the administrator had to consider arrangements for its payment. The Court did not hold that an unpaid balance alone necessarily prevents distribution or completes the inquiry.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 53 and 55 of the Estate Duty Act, the executor is accountable for estate duty and must account for the estate passing on death; the executor's responsibility to make satisfactory arrangements for payment is relevant to whether administration is complete. The Court relied on Leelavatamma v. C.E.D. in discussing estate-duty liability, while explaining that the ultimate incidence of the duty does not necessarily fall on the executor.

predicates.estate_administration_completion_assessm: The proceeding concerned whether administration of a deceased person's estate had ended for income-tax assessment purposes.
predicates.administrator_administered_estate: A person took charge of and administered the deceased person's estate.
predicates.estate_duty_remained_unpaid: Some estate duty assessed on property passing on the deceased person's death remained unpaid during the period at issue.
predicates.outstanding_estate_duty_must_be_consider: The outstanding estate-duty liability must be considered when deciding whether administration is complete.

issues.definition: When a proceeding concerns whether estate administration has ended, a person administered the estate, and estate duty remained unpaid, the outstanding duty must be considered in deciding completion.
